newsitem.title: USA: Florida Panthers to sell 7.3 million shares in IPO.
newsitem.headline: Florida Panthers to sell 7.3 million shares in IPO.

text.p: The Florida Panthers, the Fort Lauderdale, Fla.-based professional hockey team, said Wednesday it planned to go public with an initial offering of 7.3 million class A common shares.

The offering will be made by a newly-formed company, Florida Panthers Holdings Inc., which is a combination of Florida Panthers Hockey Club Inc. and two other related entities currently backing the team.
The offering, disclosed in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, will be made at an estimated $10 a share for up to 2.7 million shares.

A concurrent offering for 4.6 million shares will be made to certain investors, including the company's directors and officers, at an estimated $9.65 a share, reflecting underwritng discounts and commissions.

The offering is estimated to produce net proceeds of about $67.3 million, which may rise to $71.1 million if underwriters exercise their option for up to 405,000 additional shares. Of the amount, $45 million will be used to repay debt and the balance, for general working capital.

The company's chairman H. Wayne Huizenga, founder of Blockbuster Entertainment and owner of the Dophins football and Marlins baseball teams, is the principal holder of the class A shares. He also owns all of the company's 225,000 class B common shares.
The Panthers began playing in the National Hockey League in October 1993 and in their third season, reached the Stanley Cup finals.
